decisions.summary: _unkinked: a returning leg under 40 ft is cut, keeping the longer arm (HAIRPIN_LEG_FT removed - no code read it)
decisions.why: 0081 drawing page verbatim: 'where a lane turns back on itself, a returning leg under 40 ft is cut'; the implementation moves to the research (FR-004).

decisions.summary: _unkinked: a hairpin whose returning leg is 40 ft or more is cut too (the shorter arm goes), claimed as a GUESS on 0081; the case filed E4 research-first (audit/found-wave45.jsonl); the test asserts the 50 ft leg goes
decisions.why: Round 1's finding answered by one of the two routes it named. 0081 opens 'A lane never doubles back in a hairpin'; leaving the long leg broke that sentence, looped the settle and let the last resort drop the whole lane. The page names no remedy for a long leg (its 'exception to the 40 ft rule' for a field spur implies the 40 ft cut does not reach it, and says nothing of what does), so the remedy is a fact the record lacks: the spec's Edge Case tiers that E4, research first, implementation changed only after. Confirmed by git show 1935f49dd: the code before wave 45 already kept the longer arm at any length, so HEAD changes nothing ahead of the research for this case - it restores the behavior the wave had wrongly narrowed, labels it GUESS (not unlabeled, not a DEVIATION rewording the page), and files the E4 row (merge.py globs found-*.jsonl into the ranking). The headline rule of the page is honored in full; nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: _unkinked: a zigzag is pulled straight - vertices ka..kb dropped, one lane from the vertex before the first turn to the vertex after the second
decisions.why: 0081 verbatim: 'Two turns of more than 50 degrees within 40 ft of path, about a dozen paces, are pulled straight'; the old cut left two lanes.

decisions.summary: settle_shapes (row 490) closes by calling the fixed _unkinked
decisions.why: Its finding is the same two 0081 sentences; with W45-2 fixed it cuts every hairpin and pulls a zigzag straight, so the settle no longer loops on a long leg.

decisions.summary: The behind-the-back-wall rule removed whole: law.ends_behind (and its LAW entry), the keeper's, tree end_faults', last resort's and Lawful's reads of it, settle_ends' carry round the gable and off_the_back, corridors.round_the_gable - including units impl-drift had ruled IN-STEP
decisions.why: 0246 drawing page: 'A lane end counts as reaching a farmhouse when it comes within 60 ft of the house, or within 12 ft of the steading's built ground'; no side is excluded and impl-drift's notes on rows 488-489 say the behind-the-house rule is not on 0246. ends_behind only ever flagged ends within WAY_END_REACH_FT of a house, so every end it flagged is one 0246 counts as reaching. Removing the law check with its repairs is the fix itself, not extra scope: leaving the check with no repair would send those lanes to the last resort.

decisions.summary: The settlement-side form (water_ways/lanes.py behind_house, reaches_dooryard, trim_lane_stubs) left for its own ranked rows
decisions.why: FR-006: a wave is a contiguous run of the ranking; those rows are ranked, in scope ('kept') and taken in their turn, not deferred or excepted.

decisions.summary: impl-drift round 1 fixes: stale 'behind a house' phrases removed from Lawful, settle_ends and last_resort's docstring (restated as 0246's reach through settle_dangling); the two doubled-tail claims CONVENTION -> UNRESEARCHED; GABLE_MARGIN_FT's docstring matched to its UNRESEARCHED claim
decisions.why: Claims brought into line with W45-5's removal and with impl-drift's own notes; the doubled-tail relabel matches its siblings (law.doubled_tails, tails.tail_doubled, already UNRESEARCHED with 'no page we read covers a way drawn twice') and no page covers it, so no finding is relabeled away from research that exists.
